items.headline: Council to consider $3.79M power-modeling software deal for Silicon Valley Power
items.summary: The City Council's November 10 agenda includes an action to delegate authority to the City Manager to sign an agreement with cQuant.io, Inc. for generation resource modeling software for Silicon Valley Power. The maximum compensation is $3,791,855 over a ten-year term.

items.headline: Planning Commission to review 251-unit Eden Housing project on N. Wolfe Road
items.summary: The Planning Commission is scheduled to consider architectural and site approval and tree removal permits for a 251-unit residential development at 10333 N. Wolfe Road, applicant Eden Housing. The plans include trail improvements and the removal and replacement of 117 protected trees.

items.headline: Commission to consider 363 apartments replacing offices on Stevens Creek Blvd
items.summary: The Planning Commission is scheduled to review The Hanover Company's proposal for a 363-unit apartment development at 19220-19300 Stevens Creek Boulevard, replacing existing office buildings. The site is on Sites 5 and 6 of the city's Priority Housing Sites in its 6th Cycle Housing Element, and the project uses SB 330 and State Density Bonus law. The agenda also lists a parcel map and a tree removal permit.

items.headline: Historic-listed Washington Street home eyed for 1,200 sq ft backyard unit
items.summary: The Historical and Landmarks Commission's November 5 agenda listed a public hearing on a recommendation for a 1,200-square-foot detached accessory dwelling unit and a 347-square-foot detached garage at 1391 Washington Street (PLN26-00020). The property is on the city's Historic Resource Inventory, so the alteration needs historic review. The project was listed as categorically exempt from CEQA.

items.headline: Landmarks commission to pick a member for historic ordinance consultant panel
items.summary: The November 5 agenda listed the selection of one commissioner to serve on the review board choosing a consultant for the update of Santa Clara's Historic Preservation Ordinance. The agenda's subcommittee roster also showed several vacant seats, including the Arts and Historic Consortium and the Historic Preservation Society liaison roles.

items.headline: Campbell Tech Park project: traffic fix limited to crosswalks; redwoods slated for removal
items.summary: City staff said the only required traffic mitigation for the 290-home project is a mid-block crosswalk and an upgraded crossing on Campbell Technology Park. The traffic study projected the project would add about 2 vehicles to an already over-capacity 30-vehicle queue at Curtner/White Oaks/Camden. Paseo de Palomas residents asked that redwoods along their fence line be saved, and council members voiced concern about losing them. The developer also agreed to record easements for a possible future pedestrian bridge over Highway 17, though no funding or feasibility study exists yet.

items.headline: Campbell renews police recruitment contract at $175,000 without competitive bidding
items.summary: On November 2, the council unanimously approved a one-year contract with All Star Talent for online police recruitment, waiving bidding requirements. Police said applications rose from about 57 in 2022 to 355 last year, with 42 hires since 2023, 32 still employed, and 11 police officer positions filled. A council member questioned whether the program favors quantity over quality.

items.headline: White Oaks Manor residents push back on townhomes in single-family neighborhoods
items.summary: During public comment on November 2, residents of the White Oaks Manor neighborhood opposed a 14-townhome project replacing three single-family homes. They said they support a housing and demolition control ordinance and asked whether the city can limit redevelopment once its housing element targets are met. They referenced a Planning Commission hearing on a demolition ordinance on October 27.
